Repair note: [issue key] · [one-line summary]

File this note only when the finding provider cannot reach a solution, or after three failed, evidence-based repair attempts on the same issue. Three unrelated issues never qualify. Fill every field. Write UNKNOWN when a fact is unknown, and never paste secrets or protected data. This note is intake evidence, not an issued order. Policy: provider-owned repairs.

1. Issue key and title
[A one-line summary naming the subsystem and the symptom, plus the stable issue key.]
2. Priority and deadline
[P0: safety, security or data loss, or all work blocked. P1: blocks the critical path or a committed deadline. P2: blocks or degrades a non-critical task. P3: minor, with a workaround. State the deadline in America/Los_Angeles and UTC, or none.]
3. Trigger
[Which condition applies: 2(a) cannot reach a solution (and why), or 2(b) three failed attempts on the same issue.]
4. Use case
[What the provider, user or system was trying to achieve, and why it matters.]
5. Scope
[Affected components, files and paths, tasks, orders and projects; what is in scope and what is explicitly out of scope.]
6. Context
[Project, task and order IDs and lineage; repository and branch with commit or file hashes; host and OS build; tool, runtime and model versions; provider, model and session (or UNKNOWN); the responsible writer and any active writers.]
7. Expected versus actual
[The expected behaviour, and the actual behaviour with sanitized error text.]
8. All three failures
[For each one: time (UTC), the exact command or action, the observed result or error, and an evidence path with SHA-256 or receipt ID. Under 2(a), list every failure that occurred.]
9. What was tried
[For each failed attempt: the remedy applied, the reasoning or evidence behind it, how it was verified, and why it failed. Also list remedies considered but not tried, and why.]
10. Diagnosis
[The known cause versus hypotheses, what has been ruled out, and the confidence level.]
11. Reproduction
[Minimal steps and environment. For intermittent failures, give frequency and conditions. Say whether the failure is reproducible right now.]
12. Research done
[Firecrawl, Perplexity or REA queries and receipts, plus primary sources consulted, with relevance noted.]
13. Effects and current state
[Changes made, side effects, rollback status, unresolved or ambiguous effects that must not be replayed, and the current state of the worktree or system.]
14. Impact and workaround
[Who or what is blocked, whether a downstream dependency is affected, and any safe workaround in use.]
15. Limits and cost
[Attempts, time, tokens and spend used; what remains; holds, permissions and budgets in force.]
16. Duplicate check
[Related issues, orders, PRs or prior repair notes searched, and whether this is new or a continuation.]
17. Decision or help needed
[The exact decision, access, tool, information or expertise that would unblock the issue.]
18. Recommended next step
[A proposed remedy and a suitable owner or provider, with acceptance criteria to prove the fix.]
19. Reporter
[The provider, model and session that filed the note, a UTC timestamp, and the intake route used.]
Template only. It grants no attempts, permissions, spend or review authority.
